name: Acquiring Ruin
gm: You start every session with a number of Ruin equal to the number of players. You can have a maximum Ruin of twice the number of players. Ruin doesn’t carry across sessions, and you discard any Ruin gained when the pool is at its maximum — just like Glory, Ruin is use-or-lose!

rows.name: A player fails a Corruption Test.
A player fails a Fear Test.
You roll a 6 on the Wrath Die.
A Complication, taken as Ruin
rows.text: If you don’t want to interrupt the flow of the game, simply award the GM a point of Ruin

rows.name: Fail Forward: a player takes Ruin for the GM instead of failing
rows.text:
Alternatively, a GM can offer a player a choice of failing or taking one of the options below.
• The GM gains 1 Ruin.

name: Spending Ruin
gm: Ruin should not be spent to punish anyone — we’re all at the table to have fun.

rows.name: Reroll Failures
rows.text: You can spend 1 Ruin to reroll failures (but not Complications) on any Test for an NPC.

rows.name: Seize The Initiative
rows.text: You can spend 1 Ruin to Seize the Initiative (p.177). You can’t Seize the Initiative more than once per turn.

rows.name: Restore Shock
rows.text: The GM can spend 1 Ruin to restore 1d3+3 of an NPC’s Shock. Doing so counts as an Action for that NPC.

rows.name: Roll Determination
rows.text: The GM can spend 1 Ruin to make a Determination roll (p.196).

name: Glory Points
gm: As a group resource, it helps to discuss rules for using Glory with your players. Glory can speed up play and dramatically swing combat the group’s way.

rows.name: A particularly impressive feat
rows.text: You might want to award players Glory for particularly impressive feats.
